tier1.text: Each obturator externus turns the thigh outward at the hip, a movement called lateral rotation. The obturator externus lies on the front surface of the pelvis. This muscle starts at the obturator foramen, a large opening in the hip bone. This muscle ends on the femur, or thigh bone.
